Memorandum of Understanding Between EPA and OSHA for Implementation of TSCA Section 6 In December 2024, EPA and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) of the U.S. Department of Labor entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formalizing their coordination on EPA’s work to assess and manage existing chemicals under section 6 of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). EPA and OSHA anticipate that better coordination under this MOU will result in improved workplace health and safety protections for workers using existing chemical substances under TSCA and the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Act and allow for effective implementation of national workplace and environmental protection statutes. These cartels control vast areas of the country and are also responsible for political corruption, assassinations and kidnappings. But which groups are the most powerful? The Sinaloa Cartel Territory: Much of the north-west. The US government has described the Sinaloa Cartel as one of the largest drug-trafficking organisations in the world. Founded in the late 1980s, it was for many years headed by the notorious drug lord Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán. "El Chapo" - or "Shorty" - was once ranked as one of the world's richest men. His life and vast drug-trafficking empire have been the subject of numerous books and TV series. Under his leadership, the cartel garnered a fierce reputation for violence and outfought several rival groups. Mexican cartels often clash with one another, but it's also worth noting that they can form strategic alliances as well. The Sinaloa became the biggest supplier of illegal drugs to the US during Guzmán's long reign as leader, officials say. pages.text: Mexico drugs: How one DEA killing began a brutal war - BBC News Image caption, The capture and murder of Enrique "Kiki" Camarena was a brazen moment in the drug war By Will Grant BBC News, Guadalajara Twenty seven years ago, the kidnap, torture and murder of a US Drug Enforcement Administration agent by Mexican drug traffickers sparked one of the biggest manhunts the US government has ever launched in North America. It also offered an ominous warning of things to come. The picturesque Mexican city of Guadalajara is bustling with life. By day, its busy plazas are filled with street vendors and shoeshine boys. At night, the mariachis line up to play for the tourists. The country's drug violence feels very far from here and, most of the time, it is. But that was not always the case. "In 1985, Guadalajara was the base of operations for most of the major narcotics traffickers in North America," says James Kuykendall, then-head of the Guadalajara office of the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). "Many of the major traffickers from other parts of Mexico, especially the state of Sinaloa, had migrated to Guadalajara both for the scenery and for the politics: if they didn't have full immunity, certainly no-one was messing with them down there." Among the agents working out of the small office was a 37-year-old Mexican-born American, Enrique "Kiki" Camarena. César Jáuregui Moreno served as attorney general of the northern border state of Chihuahua from 2023 to this year. The involvement of Americans came to light after two US agents said to have worked for the CIA died in a car crash in Chihuahua along with two Mexican law enforcement officers. Attorney General Ernestina Godoy Ramos said Jáuregui had allowed foreign agents to carry out activities reserved for Mexican authorities and had failed to share information. Jáuregui has denied the allegations. The former prosecutor, who is a member of the conservative opposition PAN party, was arrested at the weekend. A court hearing is scheduled for Saturday. A judge must still determine whether there is enough evidence to proceed with the case, Reuters news agency reports. The microloan program provides loans up to $50,000 to help small businesses and certain not-for-profit childcare centers start up and expand. The average microloan is about $13,000. SBA provides funds to specially designated intermediary lenders, which are nonprofit community-based organizations with experience in lending as well as management and technical assistance. Close MikeHur's Diary Wandering Around: a browser game that turns OSM into a walkable world Posted by MikeHur on 3 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 8 November 2026. I’ve been building Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk around any town or city on Earth. The whole world comes from OpenStreetMap, so I’d like to share how it uses OSM data and ask this community for feedback. Play it here: https://wanderingaround.games (works on phone and desktop, no account needed) News and updates: https://ko-fi.com/wanderingaroundtheworld Screenshots and a short video: https://mikehur.itch.io/wandering-around How the map is built Streets, buildings, water, parks and bridges come from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (zoom 14, OpenMapTiles schema). The game fetches the tiles around the player, decodes them in the browser, stitches buildings that are split across tile edges and turns everything back into OSM-style features with tags. The game logic works on those tags, so it is the same code whether the data comes from tiles or (as a fallback) from Overpass. 2D and 3D: the same data drives a 2D map and a 3D eye-level view. Building heights come from OSM where they are tagged. Transit: train routes and stations, city buses, ferries and signposts come from Overpass queries, so you can travel between real stops and stations. pages.text: Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Misclassification of Employees as Independent Contractors Under the Fair Labor Standards Act A worker is entitled to minimum wage and overtime pay protections under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) when there is an employment relationship between the worker and an employer and there is coverage under the FLSA. Employers are responsible for determining whether a worker is an employee under the FLSA. Misclassification occurs when an employer treats a worker who is an employee under the FLSA as an independent contractor. Misclassifying employees as independent contractors is a serious problem because misclassified employees may not receive the minimum wage and overtime pay to which they are entitled under the FLSA or other benefits and protections to which they are entitled under the law. As part of its efforts to address misclassification, the Wage and Hour Division on January 10, 2024 published a final rule , effective March 11, 2024, revising its guidance on how to analyze whether a worker is an employee or independent contractor under the FLSA. This guidance is available in the form of regulations at 29 CFR Part 795. Introducing NPR Music's Tiny Desk (home) concerts, bringing you performances from across the country and the world. It's the same spirit — stripped-down sets, an intimate setting — just a different space. It's fair to say Mon Laferte is a musical chameleon. The Chilean vocalist's output of late has covered a vast swath of musical styles from Latin America, from big-band mambo to electronic dance club jams with a hint of reggaeton, and a few stops in between. The secret to the successes of these stylistic changes is the level of imagination and creativity she infuses in each turn. Mon Laferte makes art in confrontation. In every new project, the Chilean-Mexican artist aims to contradict, expose or challenge norms; she takes the assignment of performing in an office space as no exception. Tiny Desk Mon Laferte: Tiny Desk (Home) Concert Tiny Desk Juanes & Mon Laferte: Tiny Desk Concert "For Your Consideration" opens Laferte's Tiny Desk with a cutting jazz number. Laced with critiques of the capitalist grind, her flank of corporate-outfitted musicians numbly nod along beside her. During "No Le Regales Tu Corazón," a song of pain and adoration written for her husband, Laferte makes no attempt to hide her emotions — tears stream down her cheeks and into her mouth. He uses that voice to tackle difficult, yet poignant vignettes — of battles fought internally and others observed in the world around him. Music There's a new generation of folk protest singers on TikTok Born in Liberia during the country's civil war, Mon Rovîa was adopted by an American missionary family and spent his childhood moving around before eventually settling in Tennessee. His debut album, Bloodline, untangles that complicated lineage through ukulele- and guitar-driven folk melodies in music he describes as "Afro-Appalachian." At the Tiny Desk, backed by his full band, Mon Rovîa glides from the intimate revelations of "crooked the road." into the thumping energy of "Somewhere down in Georgia," a nod towards the South's violent history. Monitoring Surface Water Chemistry Surface water chemistry is a direct indicator of the effects of acid rain on water bodies. Networks that monitor surface water chemistry over long time periods provide valuable information on aquatic ecosystem health and how water bodies respond to changes in acid-causing emissions. EPA oversees the Long-Term Monitoring (LTM) program, which tracks changes in surface water chemistry in response to changing air pollution and acid deposition. The goal of this long-term program is to track whether the Clean Air Act Amendments (CAAA) ( Plain English Guide to the Clean Air Act ) have been effective in reducing the acidity of surface waters in New England, the Northern Adirondack Mountains, Appalachian Plateau, and the Central Appalachians and advance the science of air pollution impacts on water resources. What are Acidified Surface Waters? Acid precipitation (commonly known as acid rain) primarily affects sensitive bodies of water, which are located in watersheds whose soils have a limited ability to neutralize acidic compounds (called “buffering capacity”). pages.text: More Than 3,000 Tarantulas Were Found Hidden in Socks During a Major Wildlife Trafficking Bust at an Airport in Lima, Peru Skip to main content Officials found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders. SERFOR Authorities in Peru say they have foiled a plot to smuggle more than 3,000 tarantulas—including species not yet described in scientific publications—out of the country. After receiving an anonymous tip , officials intercepted three travelers—two German citizens and one Polish citizen—at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima as they were checking in at the boarding area. When they searched the travelers’ luggage, they found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders hidden in socks, according to a November 4 statement from the National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru (SERFOR). “We noticed that some of them were moving,” Cora Suárez , a SERFOR forest and wildlife control technician who works at the airport, tells the Agence France-Presse . “There were small ones and large ones.” Workers used slender wooden sticks to gently brush the spiders into clear plastic containers. Once officials are done investigating them, the tarantulas will be taken to an authorized breeding center. Authorities are still trying to identify all the species. SERFOR The travelers were trying to fly to Germany. Instead, they were detained by the Peruvian National Police’s environmental crimes unit and now face criminal charges. For Sandra Salcedo, who moved from Colombia to Madrid eight years ago, that connection is folded into every pastry she sells at her bakery—a place where people can come together to share memories, stories, and of course, a taste of home. But food isn’t the only way Sandra maintains her connection with Colombia. Thousands of miles away, her uncle Byron relies on the money his niece sends home every month. For Byron, who is unable to work due to illness, Sandra’s contributions help pay for everyday essentials, while providing greater stability for tomorrow. Like millions of people supporting family and friends across borders, she is helping create opportunities that extend beyond a single transfer. As Sandra explains, the money she sends home is her way of being there, and of keeping her uncle company. In her own words: “It represents peace of mind.” Sandra’s story is part of a wider global tapestry. pages.text: Moscow to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Weightlifting was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1896 Games in Athens By Craig Nelson BBC Sport Journalist Published 25 October 2026 Updated 27 October 2026 Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events. In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee. That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine. The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India. "All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones. No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine. The Clean Air Act identifies two types of national ambient air quality standards. Primary standards provide public health protection, including protecting the health of "sensitive" populations such as asthmatics, children, and the elderly. Secondary standards provide public welfare protection, including protection against decreased visibility and damage to animals, crops, vegetation, and buildings. Together with a blockbuster October study, a new throat bone analysis delivers a “one-two punch” to the 40-year debate over whether Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct species. Nanotyrannus lancensis, which recent findings suggest was a distinct dinosaur and not a young Tyrannosaurus rex , was a small-sized Late Cretaceous predator that may have competed with juvenile T.rex for food. Andrey Atuchin, Cleveland Museum of Natural History By Riley Black Published December 4, 2025 Nipping at the heels of a landmark study from October that crowned the short king Nanotyrannus as a legitimate dinosaur, a second team of paleontologists has independently reached the same conclusion: the tiny carnivore was no teen Tyrannosaurus rex but its own distinct species. The new research, published Thursday in Science , comes from an analysis of a small throat bone of the very specimen that set off the decades-old debate.
